settings.subtitle: Falken makes some of the most underrated tires in our lineup — the Wildpeak A/T Trail and A/T4W are 3PMSF-rated and punch well above their price. We also stock the Aklimate A/W all-weather at 111 42 Ave SW.
settings.intro_heading: Why we recommend Falken in Calgary
settings.intro_richtext:
Falken is the performance brand of Sumitomo Rubber, founded in Japan in 1983. They're best known among Calgary drivers for the Wildpeak all-terrain line — affordable 3PMSF-rated tires that often outperform their price tag in tread life and wet/snow grip.

The Wildpeak A/T Trail is built for crossovers and SUVs that see occasional off-road but daily-drive on pavement. 3PMSF rated, so it meets Alberta's winter-tire law and the BC Highway 93 / Trans-Canada Banff mandate. The Wildpeak A/T4W takes it more aggressive for half-ton trucks and serious gravel runs.

For drivers who want one tire all year, the Aklimate A/W is Falken's 3PMSF-rated all-weather option — quieter on pavement than dedicated winters, plenty of grip for Calgary's chinook freeze-thaw.

Every Falken we install gets the same balance, calibrated torque, and TPMS reset — and we price-match local Calgary competitors. Book installation or call (403) 452-4283.
settings.cta_description: Stocked Falken sizes installed same-day. Price-matched against any local Calgary competitor on the same model.
settings.faq_1_a: Yes. Both the Wildpeak A/T Trail and Wildpeak A/T4W carry the 3PMSF (three-peak mountain snowflake) symbol — they meet Alberta's winter-tire law and the BC Highway 93 / Trans-Canada Banff winter-tire mandate from October through April.
settings.faq_2_q: How much do Falken tires cost in Calgary?
settings.faq_2_a: Falken tires at Prince Tires range from $170 to $310 per tire. Aklimate A/W starts around $170; Wildpeak A/T Trail around $230; Wildpeak A/T4W around $230–$300 depending on size. Significantly less than Michelin or Bridgestone equivalents.
settings.faq_3_q: Wildpeak A/T Trail vs A/T4W — which one for Calgary?
settings.faq_3_a: A/T Trail is the crossover/SUV-optimized version — quieter on pavement, comfortable for daily Deerfoot commuting. A/T4W is the bigger-vehicle version with higher load ratings and a more aggressive shoulder for half-ton trucks and serious gravel. Both 3PMSF rated.
settings.faq_4_q: Is Falken Aklimate a good winter tire?
settings.faq_4_a: The Aklimate A/W is a 3PMSF-rated all-weather (not a dedicated winter). It performs well in Calgary's freeze-thaw and meets Alberta winter law. For pure ice/extreme-cold dedicated winter performance, a dedicated winter tire (Blizzak WS90, X-Ice Snow, iceGUARD iG53) still grips harder below -25°C.
settings.faq_5_a: Yes for most stocked sizes if booked before midday. Aklimate A/W in common sedan/crossover sizes (205/55R16, 215/55R17, 225/45R17) is reliably in stock. Wildpeak truck sizes need a 60-minute slot — call (403) 452-4283 to confirm.
settings.faq_6_a: Wildpeak A/T Trail carries a 65,000-mile (100,000 km) treadwear warranty. Aklimate A/W carries a 70,000-mile warranty. Both come with Falken's manufacturer defect coverage. Prince Tires handles warranty claims directly with Falken on behalf of customers.
settings.calgary_richtext: Falken Wildpeak A/T3W is the most aggressive all-terrain in this price band — a real alternative to BFG KO3 if you want similar gravel performance for less. AZENIS FK510 is a serious summer performance tire for Audi/BMW track-day work at the Stampede Park region. EuroWinter HS01 handles Calgary winters on European sedans at a fair price.
settings.awards_text: Sumitomo Rubber subsidiary. Major motorsports sponsor (Formula Drift, Le Mans, Pikes Peak).
settings.testimonial_quote: Wildpeak A/T3W on my 4Runner. Eastern Slopes gravel doesn't faze them. Half the price of BFG, similar grip.
